- Every dependence on an undocumented `claude` behaviour is a capability-ledger row in `viola-agent-claude` with a `viola verify` probe, never an unconditional assumption (except StopFailure, registered with no ledger row and no verify probe); Claude shapes only in `viola-agent-claude` (save the test-only live rig in `viola-e2e`, which reads the key names and the source word of its own captured UserPromptSubmit payload, never a value, and its own captured StopFailure payload's key names, error word (one of the CLI's 13, else `other`) and two text lengths, never a text, and seeds its private Claude config and reads its `cachedChromeExtensionInstalled` key name, never a value, and whose VH arm reads the real config's key names and one needle word, never a value, and the test-only fake agent and rig, which read a Claude config file's trust record); Tokio only in `viola-mcp`.

- Crate dependency direction is enforced by manifests: `viola-core` depends on no viola crate; `viola-pty` knows no agent; `viola-hyprland` is the one compositor seam (queries and dispatches only through its closed request set), sync and tokio-free, depending on `viola-core` alone among viola crates; only `viola-agent-claude` knows Claude payload shapes, including those of `claude agents --json` (except, test-only, the live rig in `viola-e2e`, which reads the key names and the source word of its own captured UserPromptSubmit payload and the cachedChromeExtensionInstalled key name, never a value, and its own captured StopFailure payload's key names, error word (one of the CLI's 13, else `other`) and two text lengths, never a text, and seeds its private Claude config, and VH, which reads the real config's key names and a needle, never a value, and the fake agent and the rig, which read a config's trust record); among the product crates only `viola-mcp` enables tokio (`rt`), and `viola-channel` lists it optional behind its `tokio` feature (the `TokioClient`), which `viola-mcp` enables; the root bin holds the subcommand dispatch, the run pump and the wheel, all of which consume only normalised events.

The only crate that knows Claude Code (test-only exceptions: the live rig in `viola-e2e` reads the key names and the source word of its own captured UserPromptSubmit payload and the cachedChromeExtensionInstalled key name, never a value, and its own captured StopFailure payload's key names, error word (one of the CLI's 13, else `other`) and two text lengths, never a text, and seeds its private Claude config; VH reads the real config's key names and a needle, never a value; the fake agent and the rig read a config's trust record). It parses hook payloads tolerantly and maps each hook to a normalised kind. It maps dialog answers to decision bodies (S3 / S7 / S8) and applies the R8 `CLAUDE*` strip. It resolves the child program (`resolve_program`: a given path as given, a bare name on `PATH`) and holds the Claude-specific half of the CLI version gate: the capability ledger rows (compiled) with their `viola verify` checks, `parse_version`, the stamp merge and `verified` verdict, and the fixture scrub. The gate's spawn is the root bin's `run::version_gate`; the stamps I/O is `viola_state::stamps`. It keeps the vt100 screen signatures (readiness gate), parses, in the pure `agents` module, a `claude agents --json` answer (`parse` into rows or a closed `AgentsFailure`, `oversize` · `malformed`; the read itself is the root bin's `run::agents`), and normalises `prompt-submitted` (removes the long-paste wrapper, then reverses tag escaping; classifies `origin` driver/human/harness). It also holds the resume shapes `viola revive` launches with (`viola verify`'s Run E is the second caller of `resume_args(id, false)`): `PROGRAM` (`claude`), `RESUME_FLAG`, `FORK_SESSION_FLAG`, `is_session_id` (36 characters, hyphens at offsets 8, 13, 18, 23, ASCII hex elsewhere) and `resume_args(id, fork)`; it is the one product home of the two flag literals. It also holds the pure `marketplace` module, `viola plugin install`'s three documents built by `serde_json` (`marketplace_files`; `NAME` the marketplace `viola`, `PLUGIN_REF` `viola@viola`; its `.mcp.json` registers the MCP server `viola`, no hooks). No adapter trait yet: a second agent arrives as a sibling `viola-agent-<name>` crate, at which point the adapter trait is extracted into `viola-core`.

- Answers `--version` like the real CLI. Standing as `hyprctl` by its own file name (in a test-scoped bin dir, in place of the real `hyprctl`; viola-hyprland's own unit tests serve `hyprctl` by a planted shell stub instead, because cargo-mutants runs only the mutated package's tests, so a root-package test cannot kill that crate's mutants), it reads its mode and reply set from files beside its exe, never from the env. It reads hook commands from `<plugin-dir>/hooks/hooks.json` (the `--plugin-dir` `run` passes), and under `--settings-hooks <file>` from that Claude settings file too, its hooks run beside the plugin's (a command string with no args split on spaces, never run through a shell). Only an absolute exec-form `command` is spawned: no shell, no PATH; a group's `matcher` is evaluated against a tool-bearing payload's `tool_name` (`hook_commands(…, tool)`). A non-absolute command is receipted `command_absolute:false, ran:false` and never run. The payload is `<fixtures>/<cli-version>/<Event>.<variant>.json`, with only `prompt` set for UserPromptSubmit and the fixture's trailing newline kept, so the recorded prompt yields the recorded bytes; under `--resume <id>` the launch SessionStart is the set's recorded `SessionStart.resume-1.json` when the set holds it, else its recorded `SessionStart.default` (a set without the variant), with `source` `resume` and `session_id` the id given (with `--fork-session`, the compiled fork id), and no other payload is built save the compact replay's `SessionStart.compact-1` under `--framing`, whose `session_id` is set to the last SessionStart the agent fired, and under `--transcript` the launch SessionStart's `transcript_path`.
